rv.q: Surely, it would be more rewarding than being the fixed if towering center of a shrine.
Frank Langella delivers a performance of such towering integrity and quiet power that it transforms Robert Bolt's somewhat static play into a riveting examination of conscience versus convenience.
Langella takes his artistry to new heights — and could easily earn his fourth Tony.
That Langella renders the role so humanly that we can identify with him is the reason to see this revival at Theatre.

cn.t: Langella delivers a towering, magnetic performance that nearly compensates for Bolt's static, respectful but somewhat musty biodrama about Thomas More's martyrdom.

vs.sum: Completed a major renovation in early 2026 with all seats replaced and legroom expanded, making it one of Broadway's most comfortable and modern houses. New restrooms significantly reduce intermission wait times.

acc.note: Elevators to all levels. 53 assistive listening devices. 11 wheelchair seats across Orchestra and Balcony.
